input.passage: The Okavango Delta in Botswana is unusual among the world's large deltas: rather than emptying into an ocean, its waters spread across the Kalahari Desert and largely evaporate. The annual flood, fed by rains that fall months earlier in the Angolan highlands roughly 1,000 kilometers to the ______ the delta during the region's dry season, when wildlife from the surrounding arid lands converges on its channels and lagoons.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The annual flood"이고 동사는 "reaches"이다. 그 사이의 "fed by ... to the northwest"는 앞쪽 쉼표로 시작된 비필수 수식어이므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론 뒤에 독립절이 와야 하는데 "reaches the delta..."에는 주어가 없어 틀리다. B는 "and"가 연결할 앞의 동사가 없고 주어와 동사 사이에 불필요한 접속사를 넣었으므로 틀리다. D는 수식어를 닫는 쉼표가 빠져 문장 구조가 흐트러진다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The annual flood," and its verb is "reaches." The phrase "fed by ... to the northwest" between them is a nonessential modifier that opens with a comma, so it must also close with a comma. That makes C correct. A is wrong because a semicolon must be followed by an independent clause, and "reaches the delta..." has no subject. B is wrong because there is no earlier verb for "and" to join, so it puts an unneeded conjunction between the subject and verb. D is wrong because it leaves out the comma that closes the modifier, which breaks the sentence structure.
input.design: 긴 분사 수식어가 주어와 동사를 갈라 놓아 독립절 경계처럼 보이게 했고, 세미콜론·접속사 오답이 그럴듯해 보이도록 만들었다.

input.passage: Ecologist Mariela Ortíz tracked how leafcutter ants in a Costa Rican forest respond when their underground fungus gardens are contaminated by a parasitic mold. Rather than abandoning the colony's chambers, specialized worker ants, the smallest members of the colony, physically remove infected fragments of fungus and carry them to distant refuse ______ they also coat healthy fungus with antimicrobial secretions produced by bacteria living on their bodies.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'specialized worker ants ... remove ... and carry them to distant refuse piles'는 독립절이고, 뒤의 'they also coat healthy fungus ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙여 run-on 문장이 된다. D는 등위접속사 and를 쓴 점은 맞지만 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 절 사이를 잘못 끊는다.
input.explanation_en: The part before the blank ("specialized worker ants ... remove ... and carry them to distant refuse piles") is an independent clause, and the part after it ("they also coat healthy fungus ...") is also an independent clause because it has its own subject and verb. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A connects the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between them at all, so you get a run-on sentence. D correctly adds the conjunction "and," but the extra comma after "and" doesn't belong there and wrongly splits the sentence.
input.design: 빈칸 앞에 동격 삽입구와 복합 동사구를 두어 절 경계를 흐리게 했고, 쉼표·무부호·'and' 뒤 불필요 쉼표 오답과 비교해야 세미콜론을 고를 수 있게 했다.

content.text:
Passage: a literary-style passage (a contemporary novel written in a 19th-century mood). It tests a clause boundary that follows a nonessential appositive set off by dashes.

Draft: "The narrator of Imogen Hale's novel The Lamplighter's Ledger—a widowed clerk who records every visitor to a fog-bound coastal inn—rarely comments on what he sees______ he simply lists names, arrival times, and the condition of each guest's boots, leaving readers to infer the drama."

Answer: a semicolon. Two independent clauses follow, and "he simply lists" restates the first clause. Options:
A) sees, (comma splice)
B) sees;
C) sees, and,
D) sees

C would be "sees, and, he simply..." — the comma after "and" is wrong. That works.

input.passage: The narrator of Imogen Hale's novel The Lamplighter's Ledger—a widowed clerk who records every visitor to a fog-bound coastal inn—rarely comments on what he ______ he simply lists names, arrival times, and the condition of each guest's boots, leaving readers to infer the drama for themselves.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 대시로 둘러싸인 동격 삽입구를 빼고 보면 "The narrator ... rarely comments on what he sees"가 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "he simply lists ..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 등위접속사 and를 쓴 점은 맞지만 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 틀렸다. D는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다.
input.explanation_en: If you set aside the appositive between the dashes, you get "The narrator ... rarely comments on what he sees," which is an independent clause. The part after the blank, "he simply lists ...," is also an independent clause because it has its own subject and verb. A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, so B is the answer. A joins the clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C correctly uses the conjunction "and," but it adds an unnecessary comma after "and." D has no punctuation at all, so the two clauses run together as a run-on sentence.
input.design: This is a medium question that takes two steps. First, students must look past the long appositive between the dashes to find the main clause. Then they must see that the text after the blank is also an independent clause. Distractor C looks partly correct because it uses a conjunction, but its extra comma makes it wrong.

content.text:
Design: passage about a biological topic with an appositive or long modifier, then a clause boundary.

Passage: "The bdelloid rotifer, a microscopic freshwater animal that has reproduced without males for tens of millions of years, survives droughts in an unusual way______ as its pond dries, it expels nearly all the water from its body and curls into a dormant, seedlike form called a tun."

Options:
A) way:
B) way,
C) way, and
D) way

After "way" comes an independent clause beginning "as its pond dries, it expels...". A colon works there because the second clause explains the "unusual way."
B is a comma splice. C is wrong because "and" would join two independent clauses, but the second clause explains the first rather than adding a new idea. That makes C partly plausible, but the sense is off. Grammatically, ", and" joining two independent clauses is still technically allowed, so C would arguably be correct too. I need to fix that.

Fix: make one wrong option a semicolon placed in the wrong spot. Option: "way; as its pond dries," is grammatical too. Instead, alter the structure so the second part is not an independent clause: "...in an unusual way______ expelling nearly all the water from its body and curling into a dormant, seedlike form called a tun." Then:
A) way:
B) way;
C) way, and
D) way. (period)

A colon followed by a participial phrase is acceptable because the part before it is a complete clause. B, C, and D all need an independent clause after the blank, and none of them gets one. That works.

input.passage: The bdelloid rotifer, a microscopic freshwater animal that has apparently reproduced without males for tens of millions of years, survives droughts in an unusual way______ expelling nearly all the water from its body and curling into a dormant, seedlike form that biologists call a tun.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 긴 동격 삽입구를 지나면 주절 'The bdelloid rotifer ... survives droughts in an unusual way'가 완전한 독립절임을 알 수 있다. 빈칸 뒤 'expelling ... a tun'은 주어와 동사가 없는 분사구로, 앞의 'unusual way'가 무엇인지 구체적으로 설명한다. 독립절 뒤에 설명을 덧붙일 때는 콜론을 쓰므로 A가 정답이다. B의 세미콜론과 D의 마침표는 뒤에 독립절이 와야 하는데, 분사구만 있어 틀린 문장이 된다. C의 ', and'는 두 개의 독립절이나 대등한 요소를 이어야 하지만, 뒤에 대등하게 연결될 절이 없어 틀리다.
input.explanation_en: Once you look past the long appositive, you can see that the main clause, "The bdelloid rotifer ... survives droughts in an unusual way," is a complete independent clause. What follows the blank, "expelling ... a tun," is a participial phrase with no subject or verb of its own. It explains what the "unusual way" is. A colon correctly introduces this kind of explanation after an independent clause, so A is correct. B (a semicolon) and D (a period) both need an independent clause after the blank, but only a phrase follows, so they leave a fragment. C (", and") would need a parallel clause or element to join, and the text after the blank has none, so it is also incorrect.
input.design: A long appositive separates the subject from its verb, so students must first confirm that the main clause is complete. Then they must notice that the text after the blank is a participial phrase, not a clause. This rules out the semicolon, the period, and the ", and" option, all of which seem plausible at first.

content.text:
Topic: 19th-century modern social change, e.g., the 1870s Meiji postal system, or penny post. Here I'll go with Rowland Hill's Uniform Penny Post of 1840.

Draft sentence: "Before 1840, British postage was usually paid by the recipient and calculated by distance and number of sheets, a system that made letters a luxury. Rowland Hill, a former schoolmaster who had studied the costs of the Post Office, proposed a radical alternative______ a single low rate, prepaid by the sender with an adhesive stamp, would apply to any letter regardless of distance."

The blank comes after a complete independent clause, and what follows is another independent clause that explains the "alternative," so a colon is correct. Answer D: a colon.

Wrong options:
- A comma alone creates a comma splice.
- "alternative, and" is grammatical in principle, but the next clause spells out what the alternative is, so "and" doesn't fit. I still need these to be convention choices only. Another choice could be "alternative, that" — but "alternative that a single rate would apply" doesn't work, since "that" can't introduce an appositive clause after "alternative." That makes it an error.
- No punctuation creates a run-on.

Final options: A) ", " ; B) "alternative, which" — bad, because "which" leaves a fragment; C) no punctuation; D) ":". Following the rule, the options don't repeat the word before the blank.

input.passage: Before 1840, British postage was typically paid by the recipient and calculated according to distance and the number of sheets, a system that made ordinary correspondence a luxury. Rowland Hill, a former schoolmaster who had carefully studied the Post Office's actual costs, proposed a radical alternative______ a single low rate, prepaid by the sender with an adhesive stamp, would apply to any letter regardless of how far it traveled.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 긴 동격구 'a former schoolmaster ... costs' 뒤에서도 주절은 'Rowland Hill ... proposed a radical alternative'로 완전한 독립절이다. 빈칸 뒤 'a single low rate ... would apply ...'도 완전한 독립절이며 그 '대안'의 내용을 구체적으로 설명하므로, 앞 절을 부연하는 콜론(D)이 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 'which'를 넣으면 뒤에 이미 주어 'a single low rate'와 동사 'would apply'가 있어 관계절 구조가 성립하지 않는다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다.
input.explanation_en: Even with the long appositive phrase "a former schoolmaster ... costs" in the middle, the main clause "Rowland Hill ... proposed a radical alternative" is still a complete independent clause. The words after the blank, "a single low rate ... would apply ...," also form a complete independent clause, and that clause explains exactly what the alternative was, so a colon (D) is the right choice. Choice A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. Choice B adds "which," but the clause after it already has its own subject ("a single low rate") and verb ("would apply"), so it can't work as a relative clause. Choice C puts the two independent clauses together with no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence.
input.design: 긴 동격 삽입구로 주절이 이미 끝났다는 점을 가린다. 그래서 학생은 독립절인지 판단한 뒤 뒤 절이 앞 절을 설명하는 관계인지도 확인해야 한다. 'which'와 쉼표는 언뜻 보면 맞는 것처럼 보이는 오답이다.

content.text:
Passage idea: an engineering case where a dash-enclosed appositive has to be closed with a matching dash.

"The Falkirk Wheel, which opened in Scotland in 2002, solved an old problem for canal engineers. Two waterways sat 24 meters apart in height, and earlier the boats had to pass through a flight of eleven locks that took most of a day to clear. The wheel's designers replaced that staircase with a single rotating structure—two counterbalanced gondolas mounted on opposite arms of a steel axle______ because the gondolas always hold equal weights of water, turning the wheel requires only about as much energy as boiling eight kettles."

The blank comes after the appositive that starts with a dash, and an independent clause follows. So the right closer is a dash, followed by a new sentence or clause. Options:
A) axle—and
That gives "structure—two ... axle—and because ..., turning ... requires". The second dash closes the appositive, and "and" joins the two independent clauses. That works.

Wrong options:
B) axle, and: the punctuation doesn't match the opening dash.
C) axle; and: "; and" is nonstandard here, and the dash is still unclosed.
D) axle: and: the colon is wrong too.

All the options keep "and", so the choice really comes down to punctuation. D is a little weak, and an alternative would be "axle—" with no "and". But that creates a comma splice? Actually "structure—...axle— because ..., turning..." would join two independent clauses with no conjunction, which makes it a run-on. So that could be a distractor too. I'll use:
A) —and
B) , and
C) —
D) ; and (the dash stays unclosed)

input.passage: The Falkirk Wheel, a boat lift that opened in Scotland in 2002, solved a long-standing problem for canal engineers. Two waterways sat 24 meters apart in height, and boats once needed most of a day to pass through a flight of eleven locks between them. The designers replaced that staircase of locks with a single rotating structure—two counterbalanced gondolas mounted on opposite arms of a central steel ______ because the gondolas always carry equal weights of water, turning the wheel takes remarkably little energy.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: "two counterbalanced gondolas ... axle"는 대시로 시작한 삽입 설명(동격)이므로 같은 대시로 닫아야 하고, 그 뒤의 독립절 "turning the wheel takes..."는 앞 독립절과 등위접속사로 연결되어야 한다. A는 대시로 삽입구를 닫고 "and"로 두 절을 연결하므로 옳다. B는 "and"로 절은 연결하지만 대시로 연 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫아 부호가 짝을 이루지 않는다. C는 대시로 삽입구를 올바르게 닫지만 접속사가 없어 두 독립절이 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 세미콜론 뒤에 "and"를 써서 부호 쓰임이 비표준적이고, 대시로 연 삽입구도 닫히지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The phrase "two counterbalanced gondolas ... axle" is an appositive that opens with a dash, so it must close with a matching dash. After that, the independent clause "turning the wheel takes..." needs a coordinating conjunction to join it to the first clause. A does both: its dash closes the appositive, and "and" links the two independent clauses. B links the clauses correctly, but it closes a dash-opened interruption with a comma, so the punctuation doesn't match. C closes the appositive correctly but has no conjunction, which leaves two independent clauses run together. D puts "and" after a semicolon, which is nonstandard here, and it never closes the dash.
input.design: To answer, students have to check two things: that the appositive opened with a dash is closed with a dash, and that the two independent clauses are joined. B and C each get one of these right, so students must compare them to rule them out.

content.text:
Design: literary passage about a modern novel with 19th-century atmosphere. Need a boundary after an appositive/long modifier.

Passage: "In Marisol Okafor's novel *The Lamplighter's Daughter*, the narrator, a widowed seamstress who keeps a ledger of every visitor to her rented rooms ______ records not only names and dates but also the weather on each day, a habit that lends the book the patient texture of a Victorian serial."

The blank closes the nonessential appositive, so it needs a comma: "rooms, records." Options:
A) rooms; records (semicolon, wrong)
B) rooms records (missing closing comma)
C) rooms, records (correct)
D) rooms—records (the appositive opened with a comma, so a dash can't close it)

All four options start with "rooms", but the instruction says the word before the blank shouldn't be repeated. So I'll put the blank right after "rooms", with options just the punctuation plus "records".

input.passage: In Marisol Okafor's 2019 novel The Lamplighter's Daughter, set in a fog-bound harbor town, the narrator, a widowed seamstress who keeps a careful ledger of every visitor to her rented rooms______ not only names and dates but also the weather on each day, a habit that gives the book the patient, gaslit texture of a Victorian serial.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "the narrator"이고 동사는 "records"이다. 그 사이에 "a widowed seamstress ... rooms"라는 비필수 동격어구가 쉼표로 시작되었으므로, 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 세미콜론은 독립절 두 개를 연결할 때 쓰는데, 앞부분은 동사가 없어 독립절이 아니다. B는 동격어구를 닫는 쉼표가 없어 "rooms records"처럼 주어와 동사가 잘못 이어진다. D의 대시는 동격어구를 닫을 수는 있지만, 쉼표로 시작한 삽입구를 대시로 닫으면 부호가 짝이 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "the narrator," and its verb is "records." Between them is a nonessential appositive ("a widowed seamstress ... rooms") that opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma as well. That makes C correct. A uses a semicolon, which joins two independent clauses, but the text before the blank has no main verb, so it is not an independent clause. B leaves out the closing comma, which runs the appositive straight into the verb ("rooms records"). D uses a dash, which can close an appositive, but an appositive that opens with a comma can't close with a dash because the punctuation has to match.
input.design: I placed a long nonessential appositive with an embedded relative clause between the subject and the verb. Students who skim may read the appositive as a complete clause and choose the semicolon, or they may miss the opening comma and choose the dash.

content.text:
Design: passage about a lake or delta. A nonessential appositive with dashes needs a matching close. Example:

"The Okavango Delta—an inland wetland that forms when seasonal floodwaters spread across Botswana's Kalahari Basin______ never reaches the sea; its water instead evaporates or seeps into the sand."

The appositive opens with a dash, so it must close with a dash: "Basin—never". Wrong options: "Basin, never" (mixed punctuation), "Basin; never", "Basin never". The rule says the options shouldn't repeat the word before the blank, so they will be punctuation only: "—", ",", ";", and no punctuation. To make it medium, I'll add a comma inside the appositive so the comma option looks tempting.

Passage: "The Okavango Delta—a vast inland wetland that, unlike most deltas, forms where a river spreads across the dry Kalahari Basin______ never empties into an ocean. Instead, nearly all of its water evaporates, is used by plants, or seeps into the sand."

Options: A ";" B "," C no punctuation D "—". Since one option is blank, I'll present it as "never" content? The rule bans repeating the word before the blank, but repeating the word after it is allowed. So the options will be: A "; never" B ", never" C "never" D "—never".

input.passage: The Okavango Delta—a vast inland wetland that, unlike most river deltas, forms where the Okavango River fans out across the dry Kalahari Basin______ empties into no ocean at all. Instead, nearly all of its water evaporates, is absorbed by plants, or seeps into the sand.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 'a vast inland wetland ... Kalahari Basin'은 주어 'The Okavango Delta'를 설명하는 비필수 동격 표현이고, 대시로 시작했으므로 대시로 닫아야 주어와 동사 'empties'가 바르게 이어집니다. 따라서 D가 정답입니다. B는 동격 안에 쉼표가 있어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 대시로 연 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫아 문장부호가 짝을 이루지 않습니다. A는 세미콜론 앞부분이 동사 없는 불완전한 구여서 독립절을 이어 주는 세미콜론을 쓸 수 없습니다. C는 삽입구를 닫는 문장부호가 없어 주어와 동격 표현의 경계가 드러나지 않습니다.
input.explanation_en: The phrase "a vast inland wetland ... Kalahari Basin" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject "The Okavango Delta." Because it opens with a dash, it must also close with a dash so the subject connects correctly to the verb "empties." That makes D the correct answer. B may look tempting because the appositive already contains commas, but it closes a dash-opened interruption with a comma, so the punctuation doesn't match. A is wrong because the text before the semicolon is an incomplete phrase with no main verb, and a semicolon must join two independent clauses. C leaves out the closing punctuation, so nothing marks where the appositive ends.
input.design: 긴 동격 삽입구 안에 쉼표 삽입구를 넣어 쉼표 선택지를 유인으로 만들었다. 정답을 고르려면 여는 대시를 확인한 뒤 같은 대시로 닫아야 한다는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다.

input.passage: In Mirela Vos's novel The Lamplighter's Ledger, the widowed innkeeper Agathe Brühl keeps a careful record of every traveler who passes through her village. One entry, written on a night of heavy snow, describes a young surveyor who arrived without luggage and refused to give his ______ the next morning, Agathe found the guest room empty, its bed untouched and its window open to the frozen road.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "One entry ... refused to give his name"은 독립절이고, 뒤의 "the next morning, Agathe found the guest room empty..."도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 D가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 접속사만 써서 "his name and the next morning"이 하나의 목적어처럼 읽히며 두 절이 부적절하게 이어진다(run-on). A는 접속사 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 "and"와 도입 부사구 "the next morning" 사이를 잘못 끊는다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "One entry ... refused to give his name," is an independent clause, and so is the text after it, "the next morning, Agathe found the guest room empty...". You can join two independent clauses with a semicolon, so D is correct. B joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C uses "and" with no punctuation, so "his name and the next morning" at first reads like a single object, and the two clauses run together. A puts an unneeded comma after "and," which wrongly separates the conjunction from the introductory phrase "the next morning."
input.design: 빈칸 앞에 긴 관계절(who arrived without luggage and refused...)을 두어 절 경계를 흐리게 했고, 빈칸 뒤 도입구 'the next morning,'가 쉼표 선택지를 그럴듯하게 만든다.

input.passage: Biologist Rosalind Achterberg spent three summers tracking alpine bumblebees (Bombus alpinus) on Norwegian mountain slopes, where the insects forage among low-growing flowers that bloom for only a few weeks each year. Her data revealed a surprising pattern ______ colonies nesting near melting snowfields produced more new queens than did colonies nesting on drier, sun-exposed ground, likely because the meltwater kept nearby flowers producing nectar later into the season.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Her data revealed a surprising pattern"은 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 내용은 그 '놀라운 패턴'이 무엇인지 구체적으로 설명하는 또 다른 독립절이다. 독립절 뒤에서 앞의 내용을 구체화하는 독립절을 이을 때는 콜론이 적절하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 'and that'으로 시작하는 절이 무엇과 병렬되는지 앞에 짝이 없어 구조가 맞지 않는다. D는 that절이 pattern을 수식하는 관계절처럼 보이지만 that 뒤 절이 이미 완전해 관계절이 될 수 없고, 동격절로 읽더라도 pattern 뒤에 동격 that절을 쓰는 것은 문장을 어색하게 만들어 콜론만큼 관습에 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "Her data revealed a surprising pattern," form a complete independent clause, and what follows is another independent clause that explains what that surprising pattern was. When a second independent clause specifies or elaborates on the first, a colon is the right punctuation, so C is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B adds "and that," but there is no earlier "that" clause for it to be parallel with, so the structure doesn't work. D could look like a relative clause modifying "pattern," but the clause after "that" is already complete, so it can't be a relative clause. Even if you read it as an appositive clause, "pattern that" fits the sentence less clearly than the colon, which correctly sets up the explanation.
input.design: 긴 지문 속 독립절 뒤에서 구체화 절을 잇는 경계 판단이다. 쉼표 접합, 병렬 없는 'and that', 그럴듯한 'that'절 등 부분적으로 그럴듯한 오답과 비교하게 했다.

content.text:
Passage idea: modern social change — e.g., Ottoman Tanzimat? Let's do 19th-century Japanese Meiji postal system, Maejima Hisoka. Boundary after long appositive/modifier.

Text: "In 1871, Maejima Hisoka, a former shipping official who had studied the British postal system, launched Japan's first government mail service between Tokyo and Osaka______ within a decade, the network had expanded to more than five thousand post offices, linking rural villages to the nation's growing cities."
Answer A: "Osaka;" — wait, cannot repeat word before blank. Blank after "Osaka" so options start with punctuation: "; within a decade," hmm options start with punctuation. Let's make blank include the following phrase: blank between "Osaka" and "the network". Options:
A "; within a decade,"
B ", within a decade,"  (comma splice)
C "; within a decade" (missing comma after introductory? that's acceptable actually—style). Better C: ", within a decade;" — semicolon makes "within a decade" attach to first clause, the second clause stands; actually grammatical? "launched ... between Tokyo and Osaka, within a decade; the network had expanded" — grammatical but illogical meaning. Hmm, medium should have one answer clearly. Use D: "within a decade," (no punctuation, run-on). C: ", and within a decade" — missing comma? fine-ish. Use C: ", within a decade" comma splice too. Better C: ": within a decade" ... colon acceptable. Avoid. C: "— within a decade" also okay. Choose C: ", and, within a decade" — that's acceptable. Hmm. Use C: ", within a decade;" which yields "launched...Osaka, within a decade; the network..." semantically wrong because launch in 1871 not within a decade. Acceptable as distractor with meaning reasoning. Ok.

input.passage: In 1871, Maejima Hisoka, a former government official who had carefully studied the British postal system, launched Japan's first public mail service between Tokyo and Osaka______ the network had expanded to more than five thousand post offices, linking remote farming villages to the nation's rapidly growing cities.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 이 문장에는 독립절이 두 개 있다("Maejima Hisoka ... launched ... Osaka"와 "the network had expanded ..."). A는 두 절을 세미콜론으로 구분하고, 도입구 "within a decade"를 쉼표로 둘째 절에 연결하므로 정답이다. B는 접속사 없이 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. C는 문법적으로 끊기는 것처럼 보이지만 "within a decade"를 1871년의 개통에 붙이게 되어, 첫 서비스 개통이 "10년 안에" 일어났다는 어색한 의미를 만들고, 이 구가 실제로 꾸며야 할 확장 시점과 분리된다. D는 두 독립절 사이에 문장부호가 전혀 없어 무종지문이 된다.
input.explanation_en: This sentence has two independent clauses: "Maejima Hisoka ... launched ... Osaka" and "the network had expanded ...." Choice A is correct because it puts a semicolon between the two clauses and uses a comma to attach the introductory phrase "within a decade" to the second clause. Choice B joins the two independent clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice. Choice C may look like it marks a proper break, but it attaches "within a decade" to the 1871 launch, saying the first service started "within a decade." That doesn't make sense, and it cuts the phrase off from the expansion it is meant to describe. Choice D puts no punctuation between the two independent clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence.
input.design: 긴 동격구 뒤에 놓인 절 경계를 찾는 2단계 판단을 요구한다. 학생은 경계를 찾고, 도입구가 어느 절에 붙는지도 문맥으로 확인해야 한다. C는 세미콜론을 쓰지만 위치가 틀린 함정이다.

content.text:
Need a technology/engineering passage. Design: an appositive with dashes, then the clause boundary.

Passage: "In 2015, engineers at the Dutch firm MX3D began an unusual project—a stainless steel footbridge printed by robotic arms that deposited molten metal layer by layer—and in 2021 the finished span was installed over a canal in Amsterdam. Sensors embedded in the bridge's frame now record strain, vibration, and temperature______ the data feed a 'digital twin,' a computer model that researchers use to predict how the structure will age."

Correct answer: "temperature; the data" → option "; the data" ... but the first word can't repeat "temperature". Options start with punctuation, which is fine.
A: ", the data" (comma splice)
B: "; these data" — keep it simple: "; the data"
C: " the data" (run-on)
D: ", and, the data" — that one is weak. Better: ": and the data". Alternatively, ", which the data" is ungrammatical. I'll use D: "and, the data". It's wrong because "and," puts a comma right after the conjunction, splitting off "the data" for no reason. That works.

input.passage: In 2021, a stainless steel footbridge built by the Dutch firm MX3D—a structure "printed" by robotic arms that deposited molten metal one thin layer at a time—was installed over a canal in Amsterdam. Sensors embedded in the bridge's frame continuously record strain, vibration, and temperature______ the data feed a "digital twin," a computer model that researchers use to predict how the printed steel will age.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Sensors ... record strain, vibration, and temperature"는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "the data feed a 'digital twin'"도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 따라서 두 독립절을 세미콜론으로 연결한 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 등위접속사 and로 절을 잇는 점은 그럴듯하지만, and 바로 뒤에 쉼표를 찍어 주어 "the data"를 불필요하게 떼어 놓았고, 표준 형태라면 and 앞에 쉼표가 와야 한다.
input.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "Sensors ... record strain, vibration, and temperature," make up an independent clause, and the words after it, "the data feed a 'digital twin,'" make up another one, with its own subject and verb. A semicolon is the right way to join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the clauses at all, so it's a run-on sentence. D seems reasonable because it uses the conjunction "and," but the comma comes right after "and" and needlessly cuts off the subject "the data." The standard form would put the comma before "and."
input.design: The opening sentence contains a long dash-set appositive, and the blank follows a list that ends in "and temperature." Because the list's own "and" makes the sentence look already joined, careless readers may pick a comma or no punctuation. They have to see that "the data feed" starts a new independent clause.

input.passage: In the 1840s, the Lowell Offering, a literary magazine written entirely by young women employed in the textile mills of Lowell, Massachusetts, gave many readers their first glimpse of factory life from the workers' own perspective. Its contributors, most of whom had left farms in rural New England to earn wages of their ______ the drudgery of twelve-hour shifts and the novelty of financial independence in essays, poems, and sketches.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "Its contributors"이고 본동사는 빈칸 뒤의 "described"이다. 그 사이의 "most of whom ... their own"은 비제한적 관계절이므로 앞의 쉼표와 짝을 이루는 쉼표로 닫아야 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론이 주어와 동사를 갈라놓아 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못하고, C는 "and"를 넣으면 주어 "contributors"에 맞는 본동사가 남지 않는다. D는 마침표로 끊어서 앞 문장에는 본동사가 없고 뒤 문장에는 주어가 없게 된다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "Its contributors," and its main verb is "described," which comes after the blank. The words between them, "most of whom ... their own," form a nonessential relative clause. That clause opens with a comma, so it needs a matching comma to close it, which makes B correct. A uses a semicolon, which cuts the subject off from its verb, so the part before it is not an independent clause. C adds "and," which leaves the subject "contributors" without any main verb. D uses a period, so the first sentence has no main verb and the second has no subject.
input.design: 긴 비제한적 관계절이 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어, 훑어 읽으면 "own"에서 절이 끝난 것처럼 보이게 했다. 그래서 학생은 수식어를 닫는 쉼표와 절 경계 표시를 구별해야 한다.

content.text:
Passage idea: a nonessential appositive is opened with a dash, so it has to close with a dash, and only then does the main verb follow.

"In the Atacama Desert, fog collectors ______ have supplied drinking water to remote villages for decades." Each answer choice has to contain the appositive.

Draft passage: "Along Chile's arid coast, villagers rely on a coastal fog called camanchaca. Large mesh nets strung between poles—structures that locals call atrapanieblas ______ capture droplets from this fog, which drain into storage tanks below."

The subject is "nets," and the dash-opened appositive ends after "atrapanieblas." So the blank needs "or 'fog catchers'—" followed by the verb "capture."

Choices:
A) "or "fog catchers"—" (correct)
B) "or "fog catchers,"" — a comma can't close an appositive opened by a dash.
C) "or "fog catchers";" — a semicolon would split the subject from its verb.
D) "or "fog catchers"" — with no closing punctuation, the appositive runs straight into the verb.

The blank starts with "or," not the word "atrapanieblas," so the answer doesn't repeat the word before the blank. Good.

input.passage: Along the arid coast of northern Chile, where rain may not fall for years, some communities draw water from a dense marine fog known locally as camanchaca. Large mesh panels stretched between wooden poles—structures that residents call atrapanieblas, ______ capture tiny droplets from the drifting fog, and the collected water trickles down into storage tanks below.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 주어 'Large mesh panels' 뒤에 대시로 시작된 비필수 동격 삽입구가 'fog catchers'에서 끝나고, 이어서 본동사 'capture'가 온다. 대시로 연 삽입구는 대시로 닫아야 하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표로 닫아 대시와 짝이 맞지 않는다(삽입구 내부 쉼표와 혼동 유발). C는 세미콜론이 주어와 동사 'capture'를 분리하여 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다. D는 닫는 부호가 없어 삽입구가 본동사와 구분되지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject "Large mesh panels" is followed by a nonessential appositive that opens with a dash and ends after "fog catchers." After that comes the main verb, "capture." An element that opens with a dash has to close with a dash, so A is correct. B closes the appositive with a comma, which doesn't match the opening dash. The comma that already appears inside the appositive makes this mistake easy to miss. C uses a semicolon, which would separate the subject from its verb "capture" and leave the first part without an independent clause. D gives no closing punctuation at all, so the appositive runs straight into the main verb.
input.design: The blank comes at the end of a long appositive that sits between the subject and the verb. The appositive already contains a comma, and the comma option (B) looks plausible. To get the answer, students have to find where the dash-opened appositive ends and then link the subject to its verb.

content.text:
Passage: biology. Pair a nonessential appositive with a clause boundary.

"Marine biologist Ana Ruiz studied the pistol shrimp Alpheus heterochaelis, a species that stuns prey with a jet of collapsing bubbles ______ its snapping claw closes so fast that the resulting cavitation briefly heats water to thousands of degrees."

Grammar check: "Ana Ruiz studied X, a species that stuns prey..." is a complete independent clause. The text after the blank, "its snapping claw closes...", is also an independent clause, so the blank sits at a clause boundary.

Possible punctuation:
- Comma alone: comma splice, wrong.
- Colon: works, since the second clause explains how the bubbles form.
- Semicolon: also works, so I can only include one of colon or semicolon.
- Dash: also could work, so I'll leave it out.

Options:
A) bubbles, its — comma splice
B) bubbles; and its — a semicolon followed by "and" is nonstandard
C) bubbles, and, its — wrong comma after "and"
D) bubbles: its — correct

B is somewhat arguable, but the SAT treats it as wrong. I need to avoid repeating "bubbles" at the start of each option, so the options will begin with the punctuation mark (e.g., ": its").

input.passage: Biologist Ana Ruiz has spent years studying the bigclaw snapping shrimp Alpheus heterochaelis, a small crustacean that stuns passing prey with a jet of collapsing bubbles rather than with its pincer ______ when its enlarged claw snaps shut, water rushes out so fast that a cavitation bubble forms and bursts, producing a loud crack and a brief flash of heat.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: "a small crustacean ... rather than with its pincer"는 동격 수식어이므로 빈칸 앞의 "Biologist Ana Ruiz ... studying ..."까지가 하나의 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤의 "when ... water rushes out ..."도 독립절이다. 뒤 절은 거품이 어떻게 생기는지 설명하므로 콜론으로 연결한 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. B는 세미콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 and를 붙여 표준 용법에 맞지 않는다. C는 and와 when 사이에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣었다.
input.explanation_en: The phrase "a small crustacean ... rather than with its pincer" is an appositive, so everything before the blank is one independent clause. The text after the blank ("when its enlarged claw snaps shut, water rushes out...") is also an independent clause. Since the second clause explains how the bubble jet is produced, a colon correctly joins the two, so D is the answer. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B puts the coordinating conjunction "and" after a semicolon, which isn't standard. C adds an unnecessary comma between "and" and "when."
input.design: 긴 동격 수식어 때문에 앞부분이 이미 독립절이라는 사실이 가려지므로, 수식어를 넘어 주절을 찾고 뒤 절이 설명 관계라는 것까지 확인해야 하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. 오답은 쉼표 단독, 세미콜론+and, 잘못 놓인 쉼표+and로 구성했다.

content.text:
Design: a passage on a geography topic with a long modifier and an appositive, followed by a clause boundary.

Passage idea: "The Okavango Delta in Botswana, one of the few large inland deltas that never reach the sea, floods each year at an unusual time ______ water from Angolan highland rains takes months to travel south, so the delta swells during the region's dry winter."

Options:
A) time, water (comma splice)
B) time: water (correct)
C) time, and, water (wrong)
D) time water (run-on)

To make the distractors more plausible, I could use "; however," as a sort of partly-right option, but then a later "so" would make it awkward. Alternative choice: "time, because" — but the rule says the options are punctuation/conjunction combinations. Since "because" would also be correct, I'll avoid it. Final options: A "time, water", B "time: water", C "time, which water", D "time water". C ruins the grammar, so it's wrong.

input.passage: The Okavango Delta in northern Botswana, one of the few large inland deltas whose waters never reach the sea, floods at a surprising time of ______ rain that falls on the Angolan highlands in summer takes roughly four months to flow south, so the delta swells to its greatest extent during the region's dry winter.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격 삽입구를 지나 'The Okavango Delta ... floods at a surprising time of year'로 끝나는 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'the rain ... takes ... so the delta swells ...'도 독립절이며 앞 절의 '놀라운 시기'를 설명한다. 따라서 설명을 이끄는 콜론을 쓴 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 연결 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 'which'가 관계절을 만들지만 뒤에 'takes'의 주어 'rain'이 이미 있어 관계사가 들어갈 자리가 없으므로 문법이 깨진다. D는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다.
input.explanation_en: Once you get past the long appositive, the part before the blank, "The Okavango Delta ... floods at a surprising time of year," is a complete independent clause. The part after the blank, "the rain ... takes roughly four months ... so the delta swells ...," is also an independent clause, and it explains why that timing is surprising. A colon correctly introduces an explanation like this, so B is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C adds "which," but the clause after it already has its own subject ("rain") for "takes," so the relative pronoun has no role and the sentence falls apart. D runs the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, which is a run-on sentence.
input.design: A long appositive between the subject and verb hides where the first independent clause ends. The distractors are plausible: A looks natural with its comma, and C uses a relative pronoun that seems to connect the clauses.

content.text:
Passage: literature domain, modern narration with 19th-century novel feel. Design a boundary question with an appositive/long modifier.

Passage idea: "The narrator of Imogen Vale's novel The Lamplighter's Daughter, a widowed schoolmistress who records every visitor to her coastal boarding house, rarely comments on her guests directly______ instead, she describes their luggage, their boots, and the hour at which they ring for tea, leaving readers to infer character from such details."

Correct: "directly; instead," → blank after "directly": options "; instead," ... first word shouldn't repeat "directly". Options: A "; instead," B ", instead," (comma splice) C "; instead" (missing comma after instead? "instead she describes" — actually acceptable-ish; avoid). Better C ": instead" hmm also arguable. Use C ", instead" (splice) and D " instead," (run-on). Fine but need partial-justification: B looks like comma with transition. D no punctuation. Make another: "—instead" without comma? risky. Keep: A "; instead,", B ", instead,", C " instead,", D ", and, instead" ... D: "directly, and, instead she" – no comma after instead... hmm "and, instead, she" would be correct. Use D ", and instead," hmm "and instead, she" is acceptable arguably. Choose D ", instead" . OK.

input.passage: The narrator of Imogen Vale's novel The Lamplighter's Daughter, a widowed schoolmistress who records every visitor to her fog-bound coastal boarding house, rarely comments on her guests ______ she describes their luggage, their mud-caked boots, and the hour at which they ring for tea, leaving readers to infer character from such details.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 긴 동격구(a widowed schoolmistress ... house)를 지나면 주절의 주어 The narrator와 동사 rarely comments가 이어지고, 빈칸 뒤 she describes ...도 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 접속부사 instead로 연결하려면 앞에 세미콜론, 뒤에 쉼표가 필요하므로 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 되며, instead는 접속사가 아니므로 쉼표를 더해도 해결되지 않는다. C는 두 절 사이에 아무 경계 부호가 없어 run-on 문장이 되고, instead가 앞 절을 수식하는 것처럼 읽힌다.
input.explanation_en: Once you get past the long appositive ("a widowed schoolmistress ... boarding house"), you can see that the main clause is "The narrator ... rarely comments on her guests directly." The words after the blank, "she describes...," form a second independent clause. When a conjunctive adverb like "instead" joins two independent clauses, it needs a semicolon before it and a comma after it, so A is correct. B and D join the two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice, and adding commas around "instead" doesn't fix this because "instead" isn't a conjunction. C puts no punctuation between the clauses, which creates a run-on sentence and makes "instead" seem to modify the first clause.
input.design: 긴 동격 삽입구가 주어와 동사를 갈라 놓아 절 경계를 찾기 어렵게 했다. 오답은 모두 쉼표 위치나 instead 처리만 그럴듯하게 바꿔서, 세미콜론이 필요하다는 점과 접속부사 뒤 쉼표 규칙을 함께 판단해야 정답을 고를 수 있다.

input.passage: At a data center in northern Finland, engineers noticed that the cooling fans, which ran around the clock even during the region's frigid winters, used almost a third of the facility's electricity. The team's fix, a redesign that cost less than replacing the fans with newer models, was surprisingly simple______ ducts that pulled cold outside air directly across the server racks took over the fans' job entirely.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 삽입구 "a redesign ... newer models"를 걷어내면 빈칸 앞은 "The team's fix was surprisingly simple"이라는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "ducts ... took over the fans' job entirely"도 독립절이다. 뒤의 절이 그 '간단한 해결책'이 무엇인지 구체적으로 설명하므로 콜론을 쓴 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 등위접속사 and를 쓴 점은 맞아 보이지만 and 뒤에 쉼표가 불필요하게 들어가 있고, 설명 관계도 제대로 드러내지 못한다. D는 that이 뒤의 절을 종속절로 만들지만 "simple, that ducts..."는 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: If you set aside the interrupting phrase "a redesign ... newer models," the text before the blank is a complete clause, "The team's fix was surprisingly simple," and the text after the blank, "ducts ... took over the fans' job entirely," is also a complete clause. The second clause explains what the simple fix actually was, so a colon is the right way to join them, which makes C correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B looks partly right because it uses the conjunction "and," but the comma after "and" doesn't belong there, and "and" doesn't show that the second clause explains the first. D turns the second clause into a "that" clause, but "simple, that ducts..." isn't grammatical.
input.design: 긴 동격 삽입구로 주절 경계를 가려 훑어 읽으면 혼동하도록 했으며, 쉼표 하나/쉼표+접속사/종속접속어 오답이 각각 그럴듯한 근거를 갖도록 구성했다.

content.text:
Passage idea: an engineering case with a nonessential appositive or modifier set off by dashes, so the closing punctuation has to match the opening dash.

Passage: "In 2019, engineers at a Danish firm tested a new kind of wind-turbine blade—one built from a recyclable thermoplastic resin rather than the epoxy used in most blades______ and found that it could survive the equivalent of twenty years of stress in just a few months."

The sentence has one subject ("engineers") and two verbs ("tested ... and found"). The appositive opens with a dash, so it has to close with a dash.
- D: "blades—" (correct)
- A: "blades," mixes a dash with a comma, which is wrong.
- B: "blades;" a semicolon cannot come before "and found," because that is not an independent clause.
- C: "blades" with no punctuation leaves the dash open, so the interruption never closes.

Rule check: the blank comes right after "blades," so the options cannot start with that word. They should be punctuation only: "—", ",", ";", and no punctuation, with the dash as D.

input.passage: In 2019, engineers at a Danish manufacturer tested a new kind of wind-turbine blade—one molded from a recyclable thermoplastic resin rather than the thermoset epoxy found in most commercial blades______ and found that the prototype withstood the equivalent of two decades of bending stress in only a few months of laboratory trials.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: "one molded ... blades"는 "blade"를 설명하는 비필수 동격 삽입구이며 대시로 시작했으므로 대시로 닫아야 한다. 그래야 주어 "engineers"의 동사 "tested ... and found"가 자연스럽게 이어지므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표도 삽입구를 닫을 수 있다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 대시로 연 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫아 부호가 서로 맞지 않는다. B의 세미콜론은 독립절 사이에만 쓰는데 "and found..."는 주어가 없는 동사구라 독립절이 아니다. C는 부호를 쓰지 않아 삽입구가 닫히지 않으므로 "found"가 "blades"에 이어지는 것처럼 읽힌다.
input.explanation_en: The phrase "one molded ... blades" is a nonessential appositive that describes "blade." Because it opens with a dash, it must also close with a dash, so D is correct. Closing it this way lets the compound verb "tested ... and found" connect back to the subject "engineers." A might seem reasonable because commas can also set off an appositive, but it closes a dash-opened interruption with a comma, so the punctuation doesn't match. B is wrong because a semicolon must join two independent clauses, and "and found..." is a verb phrase with no subject of its own. C leaves the interruption unclosed, which makes it look as if "found" goes with "blades."
input.design: I put a long appositive opened by a dash between the subject and the second verb of a compound predicate. To answer, students have to find where the appositive ends and see that the punctuation must match the opening dash.

content.text:
Topic: modern social change. Example: the 1880s Settlement house movement? Let's design with nonessential appositive then clause boundary.

Passage: "In 1889, Jane Addams and Ellen Gates Starr opened Hull House, a settlement house in a crowded immigrant neighborhood on Chicago's Near West Side______ within a decade, its residents were running a kindergarten, a public bath, and night classes for workers."
Correct: "Side; by" — wait, blank after "Side". Options: A) "Side, within" comma splice; B) "Side, and, within" weird. Let me make options: A ", within a decade" (splice), B "—within a decade" (dash alone... a single dash joining two independent clauses is arguably acceptable in SAT? SAT treats a dash can join clauses sometimes. Avoid.) Use: A ", and within a decade," hmm that's correct. Choose: A "," B " and" (run-on without comma? Actually "and" without comma between long independent clauses—SAT considers that incorrect). C ";" D "" (no punctuation, fused). Medium distractors: B partly plausible. Fine.

input.passage: In 1889, reformers Jane Addams and Ellen Gates Starr opened Hull House, a settlement house in a crowded immigrant neighborhood on Chicago's Near West Side______ within a decade, its residents were running a kindergarten, a public bathhouse, and evening classes for factory workers.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격구(a settlement house ... Near West Side)로 끝나지만, 문장의 주절 "Jane Addams and Ellen Gates Starr opened Hull House"는 그 앞에서 이미 완성되어 있고, 빈칸 뒤 "within a decade, its residents were running..."도 독립절이다. 독립절 두 개를 잇는 데는 세미콜론이 알맞으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 등위접속사 and를 쓰긴 했지만 두 긴 독립절을 이을 때 필요한 쉼표가 없다. D는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ends with a long appositive (a settlement house ... Near West Side), but the main clause, "Jane Addams and Ellen Gates Starr opened Hull House," is already complete before it. What comes after the blank, "within a decade, its residents were running...," is also an independent clause. A semicolon is the right way to join two independent clauses, so C is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B uses the conjunction "and" but leaves out the comma that should come before it when it joins two long independent clauses. D puts no punctuation between the clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence.
input.design: A long appositive comes before the blank, so it's easy to miss where one clause ends and the next begins. The student has to see that both sides are independent clauses before choosing the punctuation. B looks partly right because it uses a conjunction, and A looks natural with its comma, so the student has to compare them carefully to rule them out.

input.passage: Along the coast of northern Chile, where some weather stations have recorded almost no rainfall for decades, the plants of the lomas ecosystem survive on an unusual water source. Dense banks of fog, known locally as camanchaca, drift inland from the Pacific and condense on leaves and spines. Researchers studying these fog oases near the town of Alto Patache have found that the fog's arrival is highly seasonal, peaking in the cooler winter ______ the plants have adapted accordingly, timing their growth and flowering to coincide with the months of heaviest moisture.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Researchers ... have found that the fog's arrival is highly seasonal, peaking in the cooler winter months"와 빈칸 뒤 "the plants have adapted accordingly..."는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이므로, 두 절을 세미콜론으로 연결한 C가 정답이다. A는 등위접속사 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 "and,"가 되므로 문장부호 관례에 어긋난다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 접속 오류(comma splice)가 생긴다. D는 which 뒤에 "the plants have adapted"라는 완전한 절이 와서 관계대명사 which가 들어갈 자리가 없으므로 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("Researchers ... have found that the fog's arrival is highly seasonal, peaking in the cooler winter months") and the text after it ("the plants have adapted accordingly...") are both independent clauses, each with its own subject and verb. C is correct because a semicolon properly joins two independent clauses. A is wrong because it puts an unnecessary comma after the conjunction "and," so you get "and," with incorrect punctuation. B is wrong because a comma alone can't join two independent clauses, and that creates a comma splice. D is wrong because "which" would have to start a relative clause, but a complete clause ("the plants have adapted") follows it, so the sentence doesn't work grammatically.
input.design: 빈칸이 긴 that절과 분사구 뒤에 놓여 절 경계를 놓치기 쉽게 했다. 문장부호만 잘못된 "and," 그럴듯한 쉼표 접속 오류, 관계절 함정을 오답으로 넣어, 수험생이 두 절을 꼼꼼히 비교해야 답을 고를 수 있게 했다.

content.text:
Passage: literary narration in a 19th-century style, written in modern prose. The difficulty comes from a clause boundary that follows an appositive.

Draft: "The old housekeeper, a woman who had served the Ashcombe family for nearly forty years, kept every key to the manor on a single iron ring______ she trusted no one else, not even the young heir, to open the locked east wing."

Options:
A) ring, she trusted (comma splice)
B) ring; she trusted (correct)
C) ring, and, she trusted (wrong comma after the conjunction)
D) ring she trusted (run-on)

Problem: the passage can't put "ring" before the blank and also have the options start with it. So the passage ends at "ring" and each option begins with the punctuation.

Options become: ", she" / "; she" / ", and, she" / " she". The D option needs to look plausible: "ring that she trusted" would change the meaning. Using "ring, which she" makes a grammatical sentence with a different meaning, so it's risky. I'll keep the four options as above.

input.passage: In Mara Ellison's novel The Lantern House, the narrator describes Mrs. Penhallow, a housekeeper who has served the Ashcombe family for nearly forty years and who still wears the black mourning dress of a long-dead mistress. Each night she carries every key to the manor on a single iron ring______ she trusts no one else, not even the young heir newly returned from London, to unlock the shuttered east wing.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Each night she carries ... ring"과 빈칸 뒤 "she trusts no one else ... east wing"은 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 중간의 삽입구 "not even the young heir newly returned from London"에 주의를 빼앗기지 않고 절의 경계를 찾아야 한다. B처럼 세미콜론을 쓰면 두 독립절이 올바르게 연결된다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 등위접속사 and를 쓰긴 했지만 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 들어가 어법에 맞지 않는다. D는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
input.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("Each night she carries ... ring") and the words after it ("she trusts no one else ... east wing") each form an independent clause with its own subject and verb. Don't let the interrupting phrase "not even the young heir newly returned from London" distract you from finding where one clause ends and the next begins. Choice B uses a semicolon, which correctly joins the two independent clauses. Choice A links them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. Choice C includes the conjunction "and," but the comma after "and" is unnecessary and breaks the convention. Choice D puts no punctuation between the clauses, which makes a run-on sentence.
input.design: To find the clause boundary, students have to read past a long appositive and an inserted phrase. The distractors are a comma splice, a version with a conjunction but an extra comma, and a run-on, so students must compare the options before eliminating them.

content.text:
Design: passage about a biology topic with an appositive and long modifier, then a clause boundary.

Passage: "The bdelloid rotifer Adineta vaga, a microscopic animal that has reproduced without males for tens of millions of years, survives repeated drying by entering a dormant state ______ when water returns, the animal repairs its shattered DNA within hours, sometimes incorporating genes from bacteria and fungi in the process."

Options: A "state;" (semicolon) correct. B "state, " comma splice. C "state, and," hmm — "state, and, when water returns, the animal..." would be correct actually. Avoid. Use "state when water returns," — creates misreading. And D "state, which" makes fragment? "state, which when water returns, the animal repairs" — ungrammatical. Rule: don't repeat "state" as first word. So options are just punctuation: ";" / "," / "" (no punctuation) / ", when". Better: A "; when" — but blank precedes "when"? Let me put blank right after "state" and options: "; when water returns," / ", when water returns," / "when water returns," / "; when water returns" ... Simpler: passage "...dormant state______ when water returns, ..." options: ";" "," "" isn't allowed. Use ":" correct? Colon also works, avoid. Options: ";", ",", "—which", ", and". ", and" would be correct. Use "and" without comma? "state and when water returns, the animal repairs" — arguably acceptable. Use ", so that" — "survives drying by entering a dormant state, so that when water returns, the animal repairs" — hmm, semi-acceptable. Use ", which": "state, which when water returns, the animal repairs" — wrong. Use ", while" ... acceptable-ish. Final: ";", ",", ", which", " that". " that when water returns, the animal repairs..." — "a dormant state that when water returns the animal repairs its DNA"—ungrammatical relative clause. Good.

input.passage: The bdelloid rotifer Adineta vaga, a microscopic freshwater animal whose lineage has persisted without males for tens of millions of years, survives repeated drying by entering a dormant state______ when water returns, the animal repairs its fragmented DNA within hours, sometimes incorporating genes from bacteria and fungi in the process.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 긴 동격구를 걷어내면 'Adineta vaga ... survives ... dormant state'와 'when water returns, the animal repairs ...'가 각각 독립절이므로, 두 독립절을 연결하는 세미콜론인 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 'which'가 관계절을 시작하지만 뒤에 'the animal repairs'라는 완전한 절이 와서 관계대명사가 들어갈 자리가 없다. D도 'that'이 관계절을 만들지만 같은 이유로 관계대명사 that이 받는 빈 자리가 없어 문법에 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: Once you set aside the long appositive, you can see two independent clauses: "Adineta vaga ... survives ... a dormant state" and "when water returns, the animal repairs ...". A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses, so A is correct. B joins them with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C starts a relative clause with "which," but what follows is already a complete clause ("the animal repairs its fragmented DNA"), so "which" has no role to fill. D fails for the same reason: "that" would start a relative clause, but nothing is missing from the clause after it.
input.design: 긴 동격구로 주절 구조를 가리고, 빈칸 뒤 부사절 'when water returns,'가 종속절처럼 보여 쉼표나 관계사로 이어도 될 듯한 착각을 유도했다. 정답을 고르려면 주절을 확인한 뒤 빈칸 뒤도 독립절인지 판단하는 두 단계가 필요하다.

input.passage: Ecologist Mariela Ostrovsky studied how the bladderwort, a rootless aquatic plant that traps tiny crustaceans in suction-powered bladders, responds to nutrient-poor water. In ponds low in dissolved nitrogen, the plants produced nearly twice as many ______ in nitrogen-rich ponds, they invested more energy in leafy shoots that capture sunlight.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'In ponds ... as many bladders'와 뒤 'in nitrogen-rich ponds, they invested ...'는 각각 독립절이므로 경계에 세미콜론 같은 강한 부호가 필요하다. 'in contrast'는 두 번째 절을 이끄는 전환어이므로 세미콜론 뒤, 쉼표 앞에 놓인 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 연결해 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. C는 세미콜론을 'in contrast' 뒤에 놓아 전환어가 앞 절에 붙어 버리므로 '질소가 부족한 연못에서 대조적으로'라는 어색한 의미가 되어 대조가 두 번째 절을 이끌지 못한다. D는 부호 없이 두 절을 이어 런온 문장이 된다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("In ponds ... as many bladders") and the text after it ("in nitrogen-rich ponds, they invested ...") are both independent clauses, so they need a strong boundary like a semicolon. "In contrast" is a transition that introduces the second clause, so it should come after the semicolon and before a comma, which makes B correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C puts the semicolon after "in contrast," so the transition gets stuck to the first clause instead of introducing the contrasting second clause. D uses no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence.
input.design: 빈칸 뒤 절이 'in nitrogen-rich ponds,'라는 전치사구로 시작해 독립절임을 훑어 읽으면 놓치기 쉽게 하고, 전환어 위치(C)와 콤마 스플라이스(A)를 비교하도록 설계했다.

input.passage: In 1959, engineers at the Rance estuary in Brittany began planning what would become the world's first large-scale tidal power station. The completed barrage, a 750-meter dam fitted with twenty-four reversible turbines, generates electricity as water rushes in and out with the tides. Its designers faced an unusual challenge: because the estuary's tidal range can exceed thirteen meters, the turbines had to withstand enormous shifts in pressure ______ they also had to keep operating efficiently whether water was flowing toward the sea or away from it.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'the turbines had to withstand ... twice a day'와 뒤 'they also had to keep operating ...'는 각각 주어와 동사를 가진 독립절이므로 둘을 올바르게 연결해야 한다. A는 쉼표+등위접속사 and로 두 독립절을 대등하게 연결하며, 'also'가 나타내는 두 가지 과제의 추가 관계와도 맞는다. B는 아무 부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. C의 while은 문법적으로 종속절을 만들 수 있으나 대조·동시성을 뜻해 'also'로 덧붙이는 두 요구 사항의 관계와 맞지 않는다. D의 콜론은 앞 내용을 설명·구체화할 때 쓰는데, 뒤 절은 앞 절을 설명하는 것이 아니라 별도의 과제를 추가하며, 문장 앞에 이미 콜론이 있어 한 문장에 콜론이 두 번 쓰이게 된다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("the turbines had to withstand ... twice a day") and the text after it ("they also had to keep operating ...") are both independent clauses, so they need a correct link. A works because a comma plus the coordinating conjunction "and" joins two independent clauses, and "and" fits the way "also" adds a second challenge. B leaves out any punctuation or conjunction, so it creates a run-on sentence. C is grammatical, but "while" signals contrast or things happening at the same time, which doesn't fit two requirements added with "also." D is wrong because a colon introduces an explanation or elaboration of what comes before it, and the second clause adds a separate challenge instead of explaining the first one. D would also put a second colon in a sentence that already has one.
input.design: 긴 종속절과 앞선 콜론 뒤에서 독립절 경계를 판단하게 했고, 'also'라는 문맥 단서로 while·콜론 오답을 배제하도록 2단계 판단을 요구했다.

content.text:
Design: a passage about modern social change in history (e.g., railway time standardization in Britain 1840s). Blank sits between an appositive and the next clause.

Passage draft: "In 1847 the Railway Clearing House, a body that coordinated ticketing among Britain's competing rail companies, recommended that all stations adopt Greenwich Mean Time ______ within a year, most major lines had complied, though some towns kept local 'sun time' on their public clocks for decades."

The blank comes between two independent clauses. Correct answer (D): "Time;" — but the rule says the first word of an option can't repeat the word before the blank, and the blank is placed after "Time". So the options should be punctuation plus the following word: "; within", ", within", "within", ": within"? A colon works too, though, since the second clause elaborates the result. That gives two correct answers, so the colon has to go.

Alternative option set: A ", within" (comma splice), B "within" (run-on), C ", and, within" (the comma placement is odd but arguably fine), D "; within". C is a problem: ", and within a year, most..." is acceptable. To make C wrong, use "and, within" with no comma before "and". That's a compound of two long independent clauses with no comma, which is fairly wrong, but it's debatable. A better wrong option is a dash paired with a comma: "—within a year," … no.

Use the options "; within" (D), ", within" (A), "within" (B), and ", which within" (C). C becomes a relative clause, and "which within a year most major lines had complied" is ungrammatical. Good.

input.passage: In 1847 the Railway Clearing House, an organization that coordinated ticketing and schedules among Britain's many competing rail companies, urged every member line to set its station clocks to Greenwich Mean Time ______ within a year, most major lines had complied, although a number of towns kept their public clocks on local "sun time" for decades afterward.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 이 문장에서는 긴 동격구 뒤에서 주절이 "Greenwich Mean Time"으로 끝나고, "within a year, most major lines had complied..."가 새로운 독립절로 시작된다. 두 독립절을 이으려면 세미콜론이 필요하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 run-on 문장이 된다. C는 관계대명사 which를 넣었지만, 뒤의 절이 완전한 절이어서 which가 문장 안에서 맡을 역할이 없으므로 비문이다.
input.explanation_en: After the long appositive, the main clause ends at "Greenwich Mean Time," and "within a year, most major lines had complied..." starts a second independent clause. To join two independent clauses, you need a semicolon, so D is correct. A uses only a comma to join two independent clauses, which creates a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between the clauses, which creates a run-on sentence. C adds "which," but the clause that follows is already complete, so "which" has no role to play and the sentence becomes ungrammatical.
input.design: I put a long appositive near the start so students have to find where the first independent clause ends. I also added a relative-pronoun option that looks like it fixes the problem and a comma option that is easy to miss when skimming.

content.text:
Design: passage about a geography topic with an appositive/interrupter followed by a clause boundary.

Passage: "The Okavango Delta in Botswana is unusual among the world's large deltas: rather than emptying into an ocean, its waters spread across the Kalahari Desert and largely evaporate. Each year, floodwaters from the Angolan highlands take roughly four months to travel the length of the ______ by the time they reach the delta's southern edge, the dry season is well underway."

Blank after "delta's panhandle region" ... let me make it "the length of the panhandle, a narrow channel bordered by papyrus ______ by the time..." Interrupter adds the trick: appositive ends, then new independent clause. Correct: "swamps;" Options: A "swamps, and," hmm that would actually be acceptable? "swamps, and by the time they reach..., the dry season is underway" — that's grammatical. Avoid. Options: A "swamps," (comma splice), B "swamps" (run-on), C "swamps, which" (makes "which by the time... the dry season is underway" broken), D "swamps;".

input.passage: The Okavango Delta in Botswana is unusual among the world's large inland wetlands: rather than emptying into an ocean, its waters spread across the Kalahari Basin and mostly evaporate. Each year, floodwaters from the Angolan highlands take roughly four months to travel the length of the Panhandle, a narrow channel lined with dense papyrus ______ by the time the water reaches the delta's southern edge, the local dry season is already well underway.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.design: 빈칸 앞의 긴 동격 명사구 때문에 절 경계가 가려진다. 학생은 동격구가 어디서 끝나는지 확인한 뒤, 그 뒤에 독립절이 이어진다는 점을 파악해야 한다.
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 "a narrow channel lined with dense papyrus swamps"는 Panhandle을 설명하는 동격구이며, 이 동격구로 첫 번째 독립절이 끝난다. 빈칸 뒤의 "by the time ... the local dry season is already well underway"는 또 하나의 독립절이므로, 두 절을 이으려면 세미콜론이 필요하다. 따라서 정답은 D이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. C의 "which"는 관계절을 시작하지만, 뒤에 이미 주어 "the local dry season"이 있어 관계절 구조가 성립하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The phrase "a narrow channel lined with dense papyrus swamps" is an appositive describing the Panhandle, and it ends the first independent clause. What comes after the blank, "by the time ... the local dry season is already well underway," is a second independent clause, so you need a semicolon to join the two clauses. That makes D correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. B puts the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence. C starts a relative clause with "which," but the words that follow already have their own subject, "the local dry season," so the relative clause doesn't work grammatically.

input.passage: Along the rocky coasts of the Pacific Northwest, the ochre sea star preys heavily on mussels, preventing them from monopolizing the intertidal zone. In a now-classic experiment, ecologist Robert Paine removed the sea stars from one stretch of shoreline and left a nearby stretch untouched. Within a few years, the number of species in the area where the predators had been removed ______ sharply, as mussels crowded out barnacles, limpets, and algae.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'the number'이고, 'of species in the area where the predators had been removed'는 주어를 꾸미는 긴 수식어구이다. 따라서 문장에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하며, 'Within a few years'라는 과거의 일을 서술하므로 단순 과거형 C 'declined'가 알맞다. A 'having declined'와 D 'to decline'은 정동사가 아니어서 문장에 주동사가 없게 된다. B 'were declining'은 시제는 그럴듯하지만, 바로 앞에 있는 복수 명사 'species'나 'predators'에 맞춘 복수 동사이므로 단수 주어 'number'와 일치하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "the number"; the long phrase "of species in the area where the predators had been removed" just modifies it. So the sentence needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, and because it describes what happened "within a few years" in the past, the simple past form in C, "declined," is correct. A ("having declined") and D ("to decline") are not finite verbs, so with either one the sentence would have no main verb. B ("were declining") has a reasonable tense, but it is plural, matching the nearby nouns "species" or "predators" instead of the singular subject "number."
input.design: 긴 전치사구·관계절이 단수 주어 'number'와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어, 정동사 여부 판단과 수 일치 판단을 둘 다 해야 한다. 근처에 있는 복수 명사들 때문에 B가 그럴듯해 보인다.

content.text:
Passage: literature, 19th-century novel atmosphere in modern narration. Boundary after a long modifier/appositive.

Draft: "The lighthouse keeper's widow, a woman who had outlived three husbands and most of her patience, kept the parlor shutters closed even in June______ the village children whispered that she was hiding something behind them, though in truth she simply could not bear the glare off the harbor."

Need: two independent clauses. Options: "June; the" correct. Wrong: "June, the" (comma splice), "June the" (run-on), "June: and the"? Alternative better: "June, so that the" — makes sense? "kept closed so that children whispered" — purpose, wrong meaning but grammatical... avoid. Use "June, and, the"? Let's pick: A "June, the", B "June the", C "June; the", D "June; and the"? D is incorrect for Standard? semicolon + and is generally treated as incorrect on SAT. Alternatively D "June, which the" — makes it ungrammatical. Use D "June: and the". Fine.

Since options shouldn't start with blank-preceding word, blank after "June" and options "; the" etc. Place blank: "even in June______ village children..." Options: ", the village children" ... simpler: options as punctuation only: ",", "no punctuation"... but need difference. Use ", the" etc.

input.passage: In Mara Ellison's novel The Salt House, the narrator describes Mrs. Penhallow, the lighthouse keeper's widow and a woman who had outlived two husbands and most of her patience, as someone who kept her parlor shutters closed even in high summer______ village children whispered that she was hiding something behind them, though in truth she simply could not bear the glare off the harbor.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격구를 포함하지만 "the narrator describes ... summer"로 완결된 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "the village children whispered ..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 and를 덧붙여 콜론이 이끄는 설명 구조와 접속사가 중복되어 표준 용법에 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: Even with its long appositive, the part before the blank ("the narrator describes ... in high summer") is a complete independent clause. The part after the blank ("the village children whispered ...") is also an independent clause, with its own subject and verb. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so C is correct. A joins the clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between the clauses, which creates a run-on sentence. D puts the conjunction "and" right after a colon, which doubles up the connection and isn't standard usage.
input.design: 긴 동격 수식어 때문에 앞 절의 끝을 찾기 어렵게 만들었다. 학생은 두 독립절의 경계를 판단하고 연결 방식이 맞는지 확인해야 한다.

input.passage: In her 2019 novel The Lamplighter's Ledger, author Imogen Saltash borrows the slow, ornate cadence of Victorian fiction to tell a story set in a present-day coastal town. The book's narrator, an aging archivist who catalogs the letters of a long-dead shipowner, rarely hurries. Instead, the series of digressions about weather, gossip, and faded ink that fills each chapter ______ the reader into the same patient, attentive state of mind that the archivist herself must adopt.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'series'이고, 'of digressions about weather, gossip, and faded ink'와 관계절 'that fills each chapter'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 와야 하므로 D 'draws'가 정답이다. A 'draw'와 C 'have drawn'은 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'digressions'나 'chapter' 근처의 명사에 끌려 복수형으로 쓴 것이라 단수 주어 'series'와 일치하지 않는다. B 'drawing'은 분사이므로 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 불완전한 문장이 된다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "series." Both "of digressions about weather, gossip, and faded ink" and the relative clause "that fills each chapter" are modifiers that describe that subject. That means the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, so D, "draws," is correct. A ("draw") and C ("have drawn") are finite verbs, but they are plural forms that would only fit if the subject were the nearby plural noun "digressions," so they don't agree with "series." B ("drawing") is a participle, which would leave the sentence without a main verb and make it incomplete.
input.design: I put a long modifier containing a plural noun ("digressions") between the singular subject "series" and the blank. To get it right, students have to identify the true subject and also see that the blank needs a finite verb.

content.text:
Topic: modern social change history. Example: 1830s Lowell mill girls' newspaper "Lowell Offering". Need boundary after long modifier/appositive.

Passage: "The Lowell Offering, a monthly magazine written entirely by women who worked in the textile mills of Lowell, Massachusetts, first appeared in 1840. Its contributors, many of them farm daughters earning wages for the first time______ used its pages to describe factory routines, boardinghouse life, and the novels they read in spare hours."

Blank between subject's appositive end and verb: need comma to close the nonessential "many of them farm daughters earning wages for the first time." Answer: "time," with options: ", " ; "; " ; " —"... wait mismatched dash with comma opener is error. Options: A "," B ";" C "—" (mismatch since opened with comma) D no punctuation. Medium: also make D ", and". Better options: A ",", B ";", C ", and", D "—". Comma before blank word "time" — options shouldn't repeat word; options are just punctuation, fine.

input.passage: The Lowell Offering, a monthly magazine written entirely by women employed in the textile mills of Lowell, Massachusetts, first appeared in 1840. Its contributors, many of them farm daughters earning cash wages for the first time______ used its pages to describe factory routines, crowded boardinghouses, and the novels they read during their few free hours.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: "many of them farm daughters earning cash wages for the first time"는 주어 "Its contributors"를 설명하는 비필수 삽입구로, 앞에서 쉼표로 열렸으므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 주어와 동사 "used"가 이어진다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 독립절이 와야 하지만 앞부분에는 동사가 없어 독립절이 아니다. C의 ", and"는 동사가 없는 주어 덩어리를 동사구와 등위로 연결해 주어와 동사를 떼어 놓는다. D의 대시는 삽입구를 닫는 부호로는 쓰일 수 있지만, 쉼표로 열린 삽입구를 대시로 닫으면 부호가 짝을 이루지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The phrase "many of them farm daughters earning cash wages for the first time" is a nonessential phrase describing the subject "Its contributors." It opens with a comma, so it must close with a comma, which lets the subject connect to the verb "used." That makes A correct. B is wrong because a semicolon must join two independent clauses, and the part before the blank has no main verb. C is wrong because ", and" links a subject with no verb to a verb phrase, which separates the subject from its verb. D is wrong because, although a dash can close an interrupting phrase, this phrase opened with a comma, and the punctuation on both sides has to match.
input.design: 긴 동격 삽입구가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어, 훑어 읽으면 절이 끝난 것처럼 보여 세미콜론이나 ", and"를 고르기 쉽다. 대시 오답은 부분적으로는 그럴듯하지만, 쉼표로 열린 삽입구와 짝이 맞지 않는다는 점을 확인해야 배제할 수 있다.

content.text:
Design: passage about an engineering case with an appositive dash pair. Blank must close the dash-enclosed appositive, then join the main clause.

Passage: "In 1937 engineers in Switzerland faced an unusual problem at the Grimsel hydroelectric site. The tunnel connecting two reservoirs—a passage blasted through nearly four kilometers of granite______ had begun leaking water into a nearby valley, so crews lined its walls with a new type of pressurized concrete."

Hmm, I should avoid using real facts that could be wrong. Better to make it a fictional-ish case without specific claims. Let me write it generically: "When a regional utility in Norway upgraded its aging hydroelectric plant, engineers focused first on the intake tunnel. That tunnel—a narrow passage blasted through nearly four kilometers of granite in the 1950s______ had developed hairline cracks that let water seep into the surrounding rock."

Options: A) granite in the 1950s, (wrong: mismatched with dash)... The options must not begin with the word before the blank, so the blank comes right after "1950s".
